decisions.statement: A template is judged by the call that template builds rather than by its pieces.
What the rules judging a call spelled out refuse, this rule refuses built.
A constant this file declares is put where that constant's name is written.
A piece the code works out is judged as one word naming nothing in particular.
That word names a level only where the slug before that word names one.
The line refused is the template's own rather than a line in what it builds.
Which files are judged is left to the rules this rule judges by.
A directive's words are left alone, as the rule judging a spelled call leaves them.
A constant another file declares is not followed.
A value arriving as an argument is not followed.
A call whose every level the code works out is not judged.
A name built as the code runs that names no call is not judged.

definition: the rule refusing a call built as the code runs where that call spelled out is refused
